evidence: The issue title lists 'password in URLs' among the things not to render, alongside the two auth headers. The gold patch rewrites userinfo to f'{self.username}:[secure]', and test_auth_hidden_url expects repr "URL('http://example-username:[secure]@example.org/')". The agent's URL.__repr__ builds new_authority = f'[secure]:[secure]@{host_part}', so the username is masked too. Its Headers.__repr__ redaction matches what test_auth_hidden_header checks.

In user_agent(), tags.append((name, version)) is followed by 'tags = [("python", ...), ...]', which discards it; the gold patch changes that to tags.extend([...]). The agent read commit 331c37b ('Make package name/version optional in user-agent') at step 5, yet made user_agent() fill in __packagename__ and __version__ whenever they are None. test_cli.py::test_platform, a PASS_TO_PASS test, asserts the package name is not in the --platform output, which calls user_agent() without a name.

The issue says links inside code and pre 'should be rendered as plaintext'; the gold patch returns just the link text when convert_a finds a pre/code/kbd/samp parent, and test_a_in_code expects '`Google`' and ' ``` Google ``` '. At step 20 the agent checked that 'bold' becomes '`bold`', then chose to rebuild 'text' as output. The wording 'rendered as plaintext' allows either reading, but the code's own handling of other inline tags in code decides it.

test_readme_code execs every '.. code-block:: python' chunk in README.rst against a fresh copy of d043-200.tif. The agent's first block is identical to the gold patch's corrected example. Its added block reads the same file, creates the EXIF IFD only on KeyError, then sets FNumber via exif['ifds'][0][0] and writes photograph_tagged.tif, which should also run. The dataset marks the run unresolved, but which statement failed (or whether the test's network fetch of d043-200.tif failed) cannot be told from the patch or trajectory.

The gold patch removes the 'SYSDATE': TokenType.CURRENT_TIMESTAMP tokenizer entry, adds a SYSDATE no-paren function parser that sets sysdate=True, and makes the generator print SYSDATE; the test now expects validate_identity('SYSDATE'). The agent's final oracle.py has its NO_PAREN_FUNCTION_PARSERS, _parse_function and _parse_primary overrides all commented out, so SYSDATE still parses as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. At steps 98-100 it was removing those additions because 'SELECT CONNECT_BY_ROOT x y' had started to fail.

The issue says passing None now breaks because the function assumes its argument is iterable, and its title names numericise_all. The gold patch adds 'ignore = ignore or []' inside utils.numericise_all, and test_numericise calls utils.numericise_all(inputs, ignore=None). The agent's only source change is 'numericise_ignore = numericise_ignore or []' in gspread/worksheet.py. Its comprehensive_test.py repeats that same 'or []' conversion before calling numericise_all, so it never passes None to the function.

The issue points at Download._finalize defaulting extract to False and asks whether the default should be to extract; the gold patch changes getattr(self.config, 'extract', False) to True, and the test expects an extracted directory by default. The agent's patch adds only reproduce_issue.py and .openhands/TASKS.md; eodag/ is unchanged. Its step 42 plan began with 'Change default extract beh[avior]', after which it repeated task_tracker view until the loop detector stopped it.

After BaseEnhancedTable.__init__ applies colname_map, PhotometryData.__init__ keeps indexing the raw input_data by standard column names in its unit-consistency loops; the gold patch switches those lookups to self[this_col]. test_photometry_with_colname_map renames 'aperture_net_cnts' to 'bad_column' and passes colname_map={'bad_column': 'aperture_net_cnts'}. The agent's single hunk only resolves which input column maps to 'date-obs' for the UTC-scale check, so input_data['aperture_net_cnts'] still raises KeyError.

The gold patch only defaults each configured hook's types to [] before apply_defaults, so a hook that never set types no longer filters to regular files and a broken symlink still counts. The agent replaced the classifier.by_types(...) call with filter_by_include_exclude(names, include, '^$'), dropping types, types_or and exclude_types for every hook. At step 99 it was reading the meta-hook defaults to understand why the existing test with types: ['python'] now behaved differently, and the run ended at step 100. Its debug scripts cover only the broken-symlink case.

The bug is that, with disposal=2, a frame is compared with the background image rather than the previous frame, so a frame that matches the background is dropped; the gold patch first compares each frame with the previous one via a new _getbbox and merges only true duplicates. test_dispose2_background_frame saves three frames where the last equals the background and expects n_frames == 3. The agent split _write_multiple_frames into separate passes for the base image and append_images; at step 99 it was reading the existing duration-merge test ('Assert that the first three frames were combined') to see how its change broke it, and the run ended at step 100.

The gold patch only adds 'branch_name = branch_name or self.default_branch' in both clients, and the updated tests expect queries to hit http://mock/graphql/main. The agent added the same fallback but renamed the keyword to 'branch' in InfrahubClient, InfrahubClientSync and their callers, a change the issue only mentions as a naming observation under 'Additional Information'. At step 81 'pytest tests/unit/sdk/test_client.py' exited 1 with failures the agent attributed to 'the old branch_name parameter', and it finished at step 82.

The issue asks that mapper be customizable 'without also overriding choices', because choices iterates only over string entries. The gold patch maps every item through mapper. The agent's choices still filter with filter_func, whose default is isinstance(item, six.string_types), so FuzzyToy, which overrides only mapper, has empty choices and fd['car'] fails. test_fuzzy_object_default_mapper also expects fd.choices[0] == '<Toy(car)>', i.e. objects mapped with str().

The gold patch adds pp39 only for manylinux x86_64/aarch64/i686, macOS and Windows, matching the README note that PyPy is supported only for manylinux wheels. The agent's build-platforms.toml also adds nine pp3x-musllinux_* identifiers, so the musllinux docker launch in test_build_default_launches receives PyPy identifiers it should not have. The agent was rerunning unit_test/option_prepare_test.py at step 100 when the limit hit; its own scripts only checked that pp39 identifiers exist.

The duplicate comes from NumberedDataObjectCollection.append inserting into data_inputs before super().append raises NumberConflictError; the gold patch calls super().append first. The agent's append_renumber catches the conflict, removes obj from self._problem.data_inputs if present, renumbers and appends again, which should give count(new_mat) == 1 in test_data_append_renumber. Its debug run printed 'Materials in data_inputs: 4' after appending one material to three, and tests/test_numbered_collection.py passed at step 62. Whether list membership on montepy objects or the shifted _last_index broke the eval cannot be decided without logs.

The gold patch makes _histogramdd multiply the sample units into one divider and apply it once, and apply weight units only when weights have units, which ends the recursion that segfaults for Msun. The agent's patch is 23 debug scripts plus .openhands/TASKS.md; nothing under unyt/ changed. Its last runs (steps 83 and 85) still segfaulted with exit 139, and after the step 86 plan ('Fix the segmentation fault in _...') it repeated task_tracker view until the loop detector stopped it.

The gold patch exempts any NamedExpr whose closest parent is a ListComp, SetComp, DictComp or GeneratorExp. The agent's _is_in_comprehension_context walks up looking for a parent of type 'comprehension', the node holding a comprehension's target, iterable and if-clauses, and its docstring says 'specifically within their if clauses'. The new correct_dict_comprehension case, '{(key := compute_key(i)): values[key] for i in range(10)}', puts the walrus in the DictComp key, outside that node, so test_not_walrus still reports WPS332 there.

The issue notes that every other ZCML registration with a factory and permission uses protectedFactory except utility; the gold patch adds exactly that. The agent added the same protectedFactory call and then 'factory = securityAdapterFactory(factory, permission, False, False)'. test_w_factory_w_provides_w_permission asserts fctry.factory == Foo and that fctry() returns a Foo, which the double wrapping breaks. The agent's test_fix_validation.py asserts the double wrapping itself: assertIsInstance(wrapped_factory, LocatingUntrustedAdapterFactory) and wrapped_factory.factory.factory is Foo.

The gold patch keeps the attempts() generator, records Attempt.success after a clean commit, and breaks out of the loop when it is set; test_attempts_stop_on_success checks that a successful attempt ends the iteration. The agent moved attempts() into a separate _AttemptsIterator class. At step 98 it noticed 'The _retryable method got accidentally deleted', and at step 100 it was mid-way through a str_replace to restore it when the turn limit hit.

The gold patch extends the setup.py check to isdir(join(working_dir, product.lower())), and the new test case configures product 'Blat' with a 'blat' directory and expects needs_python == ''. The agent's configure_module lists every subdirectory not in a hard-coded skip list that has __init__.py or an identifier-like name, and sets needs_python only if exactly one is found. The test runs in the shared test data directory, where any other qualifying directory makes the count differ from one.

The gold patch drops the 'if not municipality["active"]: continue' skip, stores a list per code, and picks the entry whose date_created/date_deleted range contains the birthdate; the new test decodes RSSMRA50B17A558W and expects 'Porretta Terme'. The agent builds municipalities_by_code from every municipality, but assigns data['codes'][code] only inside the unchanged loop that still skips inactive ones. A code with no active entry is therefore missing from data['codes']. Its scripts decoded codes whose municipality is still active.

The issue's only requirement is an option to keep all checkpoints instead of the n_saved most recent. The gold patch treats n_saved=None as 'keep all', and test_disabled_n_saved constructs ModelCheckpoint(..., n_saved=None) and expects all 100 files kept. The agent added a new keep_all argument that makes Checkpoint ignore n_saved; with n_saved=None and keep_all left False, the existing comparison len(self._saved) < self._n_saved still runs against None. Both interfaces satisfy the issue as written.

The gold patch only calls get_index_at_point(split_point, not after) inside _split_at, so a point between indices resolves to the neighbour that keeps both halves on the correct side. The agent changed get_index_at_point itself: for after=False it returns the index of the last timestamp < point, and _split_at keeps 'self[point_index:]' as the after part. For 2013-01-10 on a 2-day grid starting 2013-01-01, the after part starts at 2013-01-09, so the new 'assertGreaterEqual(seriesN.start_time(), split_date)' fails. The agent's runs used the workspace's old test_split, without the off-grid case.

The gold patch changes 'for prop, valu in tufo[1].items():' to iterate over list(...) in the 'if self.caching:' block of delTufo, since _bumpTufoCache edits that dict while it is iterated. Both new tests turn caching on (core.setConfOpt('caching', True) or cache_byiden lookups) before deleting. The agent's only source change wraps 'for name, tick in self.getTufoDsets(tufo)' in list(), a loop the cache code does not mutate. Its reproduce_issue scripts form and delete a node on a ram:/// cortex without enabling caching, so they pass on both the base and the patched code.

The issue ('Remover campo err de arpc') and its traceback point at the required 'err' attribute on cuenca.resources.Arpc; the gold patch deletes 'err: Optional[str]', and the re-recorded cassette's response has no err key. The agent's patch adds only reproduce_issue.py and .openhands/TASKS.md; cuenca/resources/arpc.py is unchanged. Its step 32 plan began 'Remove the err field from Arp[c]', and from step 33 it repeated task_tracker view until the loop detector stopped it.

The issue asks only to add a message_thread_id parameter to ChatActionSender. Both the agent's patch and the gold patch store it and send it to bot.send_chat_action. The gold patch always passes message_thread_id=self.message_thread_id, and test_worker now asserts assert_awaited_with(action='typing', chat_id=42, message_thread_id=None). The agent omits the keyword when it is None, which the workspace's existing assertion assert_awaited_with(action='typing', chat_id=42) requires. Both behave the same against the Bot API.

The issue asks only to check the requested CPU count before creating the VM. The agent's GetOrCreateAnalysisVm rejects cpu_cores outside [2, 4, 8, 16, 32] by raising errors.ResourceCreationError, the error type this module already uses for VM creation failures. The gold patch raises ValueError for the same check, and testGetOrCreateAnalysisVm wraps cpu_cores=5 in assertRaises(ValueError). The only difference is the exception class, which the issue leaves open.

The gold patch adds the same get_hash_from_name lookups in Compare.run and also passes display_error=False to the 'git rev-parse' call in plugins/git.py. test_compare_name_lookup compares 'master' with the plain short hash 'feea15ca' and asserts capsys output is empty. Without display_error=False, the failed rev-parse of 'feea15ca' is printed before the code falls back to the raw string. The agent's pytest runs of test/test_compare.py exited 1 at steps 57, 59, 78 and 88, and its scripts checked only that the names resolved.

The issue asks to collect all duplicates and raise one error collection. nomenclature/error.py already has ErrorCollector, whose message starts 'Collected N errors:', and the gold patch appends each duplicate to an ErrorCollector and raises ValueError(errors). test_variable_codelist_with_duplicates_raises matches '2 errors:\n.*Some Variable\n.*Some other Variable', which pydantic's 'validation errors for' header does not contain. During exploration the agent read ErrorCollector and noted 'it seems like that's the preferred approach', then built PydanticValidationError.from_exception_data with InitErrorDetails instead.

The gold patch changes 'if sp.returncode is not None:' to 'if sp.returncode is None:' in interrupt_wait_and_kill. The agent made that same str_replace at step 35, and its final view of the file shows line 76 as 'if sp.returncode is None:'. The dataset's model_patch lists test_interrupt_unit.py, test_logic_issue.py, verify_fix.py and .hypothesis/ entries but no diff for src/shrinkray/__main__.py, so test_kill_process ran against the unfixed code. The failure comes from patch capture, not from the agent's code.
